title: Specify encoding, BOM, newline, and byte-count semantics

state.decision_rationale: Accepted as original valid UTF-8 source bytes with preserved BOM and newline sequences; invalid UTF-8 remains explicit.

provenance.review_target: MKTCTX/3 Continuum packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Say charset=utf-8 and name the policy. State whether bytes and range are computed pre- or post-normalization and define line counting for LF, CRLF, and other encodings.
feedback.normalized_claim: The format needs normative encoding, BOM, invalid-byte, newline-preservation, byte-count, and line-count rules before representation=exact can be interoperable.

current_behavior: Exact chunks preserve JavaScript string contents and recognize LF, CRLF, and bare CR as line terminators without converting them during chunk splitting.
Rendered byte counts use Buffer.byteLength(content, utf8), and the parser re-encodes the packet as UTF-8 before consuming framed bytes.
The format does not declare a charset, BOM policy, invalid-UTF-8 policy, or whether exactness applies to original file bytes versus decoded text.
The current ingestion path can hash original source bytes while TextDecoder decoding removes a UTF-8 BOM before rendering, creating a known exactness mismatch for BOM-bearing input.
evidence: src/manifest.ts: source buffer hashing and text decoding path
ChatGPT feedback intake repository investigation of UTF-8 BOM decoding

proposal.summary: Define whether MKTCTX exact content preserves file bytes or canonical UTF-8 text, then make encoding, BOM, invalid-byte, newline, line-count, and digest rules consistent with that decision.
candidate_changes: Declare charset and normalization fields at packet or file level and define their scope.
Specify whether bytes and sha256 bind original file bytes, decoded source text encoded as UTF-8, or a declared canonical representation.
Define BOM retention, invalid-UTF-8 handling, binary classification, and LF, CRLF, and bare-CR line counting.
Add fixtures for UTF-8 BOM, CRLF, bare CR, multibyte Unicode, invalid UTF-8, UTF-16, and non-text selections.
non_goals: Do not silently label normalized text as byte-identical source.
Do not require support for every character encoding unless explicitly selected as a goal.
Do not hand-wave encoding behavior as an implementation detail of Node.js.

questions: Is representation=exact intended to mean original bytes or exact decoded source text?
Should non-UTF-8 files be omitted, embedded as encoded bytes, or represented by a separate projection?
Are line ranges counted over preserved newline sequences or a normalized citation view?
risks: Changing exactness semantics can invalidate existing hashes and requires a format-version bump.
Normalizing newlines improves portability but breaks byte-level reconstruction.
Encoding metadata without strict decoder requirements may still produce divergent consumers.
evidence_needed: Round-trip tests over representative encodings and newline styles.
A decision table mapping input byte classes to inclusion, projection, hash, and reconstruction behavior.
